speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On 5 November 2018, an article was published on the website, the States Times Review (STR), stating that agreements with Malaysia on the supply of water and on the high-speed rail, favoured Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These arguments have been raised by Malaysia previously and dealt with before in this House and elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Singapore was the first jurisdiction to take strong action against the financial institutions and individuals involved in the 1MDB scandal.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Investigations commenced in March 2015 and have since led to serious action taken against wrongdoers.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) undertook a two-year investigation of both foreign and local banks.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This was the most extensive supervisory review it has ever taken.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As a result of these investigations, it shut down two banks – BSI Bank Limited Singapore and Falcon Bank.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Arrest warrants for Jho Low and his proxy Tan Kim Loong were issued.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Singapore also requested Interpol Red Notices to be put out for Low and Tan.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We are the first – and it seems, the only – country to date of at least 10 jurisdictions involved, that has secured convictions of individuals who facilitated the laundering.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Five individuals have been charged and convicted for offences relating to the 1MDB scandal.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Investigations are continuing into several other suspects in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On 8 June this year, officers from MAS, the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) and the Commercial Affairs Department met the Malaysian 1MDB Taskforce led by Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Singapore has been providing Malaysia information on 1MDB-related fund flows since March 2015, and this has been acknowledged by Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The information I have referred to is all publicly available.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And obviously there is no basis for the claims of corruption being made against our officials.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I move on now to the curious circumstances in which the falsehoods were then further perpetuated.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: A few months ago, in May 2018, a similar article was published by STR.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On 5 November 2018, the same article was repackaged.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It used a quote from the Sarawak Report as a peg to reiterate the falsehoods first published in May.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As at 8 November, this article had been shared around 1,600 times on Facebook.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some of these shares resulted from a concerted effort by a small group of users to spread the article across multiple Facebook groups, including groups that ostensibly cover unrelated subjects.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The shares by this small group of just seven users accounted for the falsehood potentially seen by over 800,000 users who were members of these Facebook groups.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Some of these facts and figures are set out in the handouts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If I may refer Members to the first handout (Annex 1) which has the "ST Review" on the left-hand side, you will see that seven Facebook users shared the article collectively 45 times over three days to 39 unique Facebook groups.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In this three-day period, about 800,000 potential viewers had been given access to this article.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If Members go to the second page of that handout, to illustrate a different point, this post was shared to five different groups within a span of just one minute and you will see the timings on the left-hand side of the extract on the second page.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the third page of the same handout, to illustrate the spread of the article, the reach on Facebook, just to these four illustrative groups amounted to about 380,000.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And you will see in the top left-hand box, the number of members in that group was close to 350,000.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, very quickly and very widely, this was spread.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On 7 November, this repackaged article was reproduced on Malaysian website The Coverage.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This report was then picked up by Malaysian Chinese-language newspaper China Press where it was viewed 45,000 times by 8 November, just one day later.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Two YouTube videos were also put up, translating the allegations into Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is interesting that, in this case, the spread of disinformation followed a pattern that has been established elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: A falsehood first appears on an obscure site, and then gets picked up by mainstream media, which lends credence to the claims.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will cite two examples in the report of the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods, which demonstrate these tactics in action.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as I go through the next few paragraphs, Members can refer to the second handout (Annex 2) by way of illustration.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The first, highlighted by Mr Ben Nimmo of the Atlantic Council's Digital Forensic Research Lab, was a false claim about the vulnerability of the United States (US) Navy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The false claim was first posted on an obscure website, then republished by a foreign mainstream media outlet.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It eventually began trending on social media and was then published by a significant number of prominent news outlets and tabloids in other countries.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It took just seven days for the falsehood to go from an obscure website to international news.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second example, also cited to the Committee by Mr Nimmo, related to a disinformation campaign against Morgan Freeman, after he had said that a foreign country had attacked the US using online activity during the 2016 US Presidential Election.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: An obscure website run by trolls first initiated a hashtag #StopMorganLie, while publishing the claim that he was lying.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This hashtag was then amplified on social media, including by a group claiming to be independent activists from the foreign country.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It was finally picked up by the mainstream media of the foreign country, who claimed that the counter-movement against Morgan Freeman's assertion was a "big Twitter outcry", even though online traffic using the hashtag amounted to only about 1,000 posts.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It was later discovered that the accounts of the so-called activists were actually controlled by a troll factory in the foreign country.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: What appeared to be an organic movement was really an orchestrated campaign.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We also took active steps to debunk the falsehoods and stem their dissemination.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Singapore High Commission in Malaysia stated categorically that the article was “clearly libellous”.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And this was carried in a number of mainstream media outlets in Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: IMDA also asked Facebook to deny access to the post on STR's Facebook page, on the basis that the post contains material that is contrary to the public interest, thereby constituting prohibited content under IMDA's Internet Code of Practice.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First, the post is clearly false as I have explained above.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The Sarawak Report on which the STR post was based and quoted, itself published a Facebook post calling the article on The Coverage, which had reproduced the STR article, "misleading" and "erroneous".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It later published another post debunking the false claims.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Many Malaysian publications, including the China Press, took down their articles after our High Commission in Malaysia issued the clarification.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Second, as IMDA has made clear, the post contains material that violates Singapore law.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Despite the clear falsehoods attacking Singapore, Facebook did not consider that there were sufficient grounds for it to remove the post.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because of this, Facebook's post with the false claims continues to be available on Facebook.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Facebook’s reluctance to remove the post is surprising.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In April 2017, it had said that it is "committed to doing everything   can to reduce the spread of false news to as close to zero as possible." In its written representation to the Select Committee on Deliberate Online Falsehoods, Facebook said that it "believe  that reducing the spread of misinformation and false news is a shared responsibility between public authorities, tech companies, newsrooms and classrooms." Facebook has also given assurances that it would work closely with the Singapore authorities to swiftly address online falsehoods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And yet, when there is an actual falsehood that attacks Singapore, Facebook refuses to remove the content.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Facebook has said, in response to media queries on its decision, that it does not "have a policy that prohibits alleged falsehoods, apart from in situations where this content has the potential to contribute to imminent violence or physical harm." There are many situations where serious harm is caused even though there is no potential for "imminent violence or physical harm".

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as Members will appreciate, the slow drip of poison, over a period of time, can one day result in and burst into violence.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And Facebook will do nothing about it, despite the various statements made in Singapore and elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It will allow itself to be a platform for the spread of lies, falsity, to poison and divide societies through such lies, encourage xenophobia, and profit from that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This incident, therefore, demonstrates why we cannot rely on the goodwill of service provider platforms to protect Singapore from disinformation campaigns.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It reinforces the Select Committee's recommendations that legislative powers are needed to protect us from deliberate online falsehoods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: When STR failed the first time to gain traction, it simply repackaged the same falsehoods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That was then sought to give credibility by mainstream media.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There is an old saying, "untruths travel halfway round the world when the truth is just putting on its boots".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: But on the basis of what the hon Senior Minister of State had shared, it seems that untruth has picked up pace since.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One, in relation to Facebook's action, did Facebook demote the news, the fake news, pursuant to its protocol dealing with fake news?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And let me just reiterate that STR had made the publication quoting directly from a report in the Sarawak Report, and quotes an interview granted by the editor of the Sarawak Report.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As we have seen, the spread is not just quick, it is wide.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, at this point in time, there are limited options to stem the spread and influence of such online falsehoods.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And so, to answer the Member's second question, yes, perhaps so, but there is probably a need for levers to be given so that these can be arrested, can be stopped.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And we have seen the proliferation rate and speed and the reach.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, something has to be done and the Select Committee has made recommendations to consider precisely this, the appropriate measures to be taken so that these falsehoods and the proliferation of these falsehoods which, as Mr Murali Pillai said just now, travels faster, can be stemmed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the Member's second point as to whether there has been a demotion or downranking of the article, it does not appear to us to have been so.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, as I said, our primary assessment is that rather than being demoted or downranked, it ought not even have been put up in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Png asked whether PA had qualified accounts before.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, this question was asked by Mr Dennis Tan on 17 August 2015 and we have since answered it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Png might want to check the record of the answer given by Mr Heng Swee Keat to Mr Dennis Tan.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Prior to fiscal year 2013, the auditor made a comment to say that the PA accounts on the grassroots organisation should be consolidated.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And because prior to 2013, it was not consolidated, that was why they said that it did not fully comply with the standards.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Prior to 2013, we did not consolidate statements and that is not the same, that qualification is not the same as that being a material impact that accounts are not correct or cannot be trusted.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It was a technical issue because we did not follow the accounting standards to consolidate all the accounts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if Mr Png wishes, he can refer to the Parliamentary answer given to Mr Dennis Tan in 2015.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: But I can tell you that when auditors issue an adverse opinion, it means something.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: It means they could not see, they could not verify the accounts of the grassroots.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: And those are not hundreds or thousands of dollars.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, that is why they issued an adverse report.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: If it is a technical issue, I am sure the auditors can do something about it though.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Can I just ask Mr Png whether he understands this, and if he does not understand, I can explain it during tea break time.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Does the Member understand the difference between qualified accounts and unqualified accounts?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Do you understand what is the difference between qualified accounts and unqualified accounts?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And the reason is that there is a material impact on the reliability of the financial statements?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Do you agree with me that even for unqualified accounts, you can have observations?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, there are qualified accounts where, fundamentally, the issue is whether the accounts can be trusted.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: There are unqualified accounts, which, fundamentally, means that the accounts can be trusted.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But can there be observations, where rules are not followed?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The answer, as you have said, is yes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Unqualified accounts means that structurally, the accounts can be trusted, in good order, but there are still observations and those observations need to be acted upon to be improved.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I hope I have clarified the difference between qualified accounts and unqualified accounts.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I have clarified why before 2013 – what was the qualification?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It was a qualification on the basis that the accounts were not consolidated.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And we have since consolidated that and we have put right.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It was from the auditor of PA who was auditing —

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Maybe the Member can show me the exact words of what was said.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It is just in the opinion page, if you look into the records of 2007 to 2012.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: In the first financial statement, they will put the phrase there —

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I want to make a distinction, and I repeat again, between qualified accounts and unqualified accounts.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I think we have spent enough time on this.
